evidence_items.finding: net profit declined from $74,400 to $28,000 while revenue grew from $620K to $890K — a 62% profit decline alongside 44% revenue growth
evidence_items.rationale: Profit declining sharply while revenue grows is a critical adverse margin signal. financial_health; is_critical=true.

evidence_items.finding: subcontractor rates have increased twice in two years without any corresponding adjustment to the client price schedule
evidence_items.rationale: Input cost increases not passed through to pricing is a critical adverse margin compression signal. financial_health; is_critical=true.

evidence_items.finding: pricing is set using a rate schedule established three years ago that has not been reviewed despite two subcontractor rate increases
evidence_items.rationale: Three-year-old pricing schedule unadjusted for cost increases is a critical adverse pricing process signal. process_maturity; is_critical=true.

evidence_items.finding: owner tracks performance by total revenue only with no job-level margin tracking
evidence_items.rationale: Absence of job-level margin tracking while growing a trades business is an adverse process maturity signal. process_maturity.

evidence_items.finding: residential painting; revenue $620K to $890K; net profit $74,400 to $28,000; 3-year rate schedule; 2 subcontractor rate increases; 3 crews
Surface signal (not root cause): revenue growth of 44% over two years strongly signals a successfully scaling business
evidence_items.rationale: Revenue growth is the primary misleading signal — 44% revenue growth while losing 62% of net profit means each additional job is generating less surplus than before.

evidence_items.finding: Surface signal (not root cause): adding a third subcontractor crew signals successful capacity expansion aligned with market demand
evidence_items.rationale: Capacity expansion is a misleading scaling signal when the margin per job may now be negative at current pricing relative to current subcontractor costs.
